Hi!
About showing the enemy level with their name, where do you want it to be shown? On the default enemy selection window? Oron his sprite?
Can you send me a screenshot and mark where do you want it?
About the average level thing, I believe you could set the below script call in a common event, and set it in the beginning of every battle:
JavaScript:
const partyLevel = $gameParty.members().reduce( (accumulator, member) => member.level + accumulator, 0)
const averageLevel = Math.floor( partyLevel/$gameParty.size() )
$gameTroop.members().forEach(enemy => {
    enemy.changeLevel(averageLevel)
    enemy.recoverAll()
})
See if this will work!
[EDIT] A little bit more explanation.
The script is adding up the level of all group members and divides by the number of group members, thus getting an average of the group level.
Then he is changing the level of each enemy according to this average.
If you want to only get the average level of the party by counting only the actors who will be on battle, you can do this instead:
JavaScript:
const partyLevel = $gameParty.battleMembers().reduce( (accumulator, member) => member.level + accumulator, 0)
const averageLevel = Math.floor( partyLevel/$gameParty.battleMembers().length )
$gameTroop.members().forEach(enemy => {
    enemy.changeLevel(averageLevel)
    enemy.recoverAll()
})

Ok! I'm taking a look at it right now, here is what I can see:
Spoiler:
spoiler
First of all, I tested the event the way you set it up. But for better debug everything, I removed the conditional branches, and just run the event on the start of the battle.
1 - You are setting the index wrong. On the editor, "#1 Blank" means troop member 0.
When you are dealing with
ID
of Enemy, Actors, Equips etc, ID always
start at 1
.
But when you are dealing with
INDEX
, they always
start at 0
.
That is probably why you are getting this error "cannot read property class of undefined", because you are pointing to an index that does not exist.
So, the first enemy on your troop, has index 0.
The second enemy on your troop, has index 1.
etc...
2 - I don't know where did you are taking those HP numbers from the enemies.
I guess, you are expecting that, when they change level with plugin commands or script calls, they also will change their current hp.
But what does happen, is that they only change their Max HP.
And so, you are doing a wrong comparison. You are stating on the Message Window, that the enemy has life 500 and their actual life is 100. But:
500 = MAX HP.
100 = Current HP.
If you compare 500 with their MAX HP, you will see that they are correctly.
Spoiler
You need to recover them, so they can fill their HP to it's maximum.
(But about that, I think I can also can add a new argument on the plugin command with that option.)
The class id 20, that you are using on enemies, starts with 100 hp. And that is why they all have 100 HP.

My guess is that Visu plugin is somehow using Game_Actor or another Game Object instead of Game_Enemy. And that is why "this.meetsActionLevelCondition(action)" is not a function, because it does not exist on the Game Actor.
Removing that, will make Enemies don't check if they have the proper level to use a skill. If you set the plugin parameter "Action Pattern Mode" to default, then you don't have to worry about that, you can keep using it with the changes you made.
Otherwise, try add that lines to the plugin:
JavaScript:
Game_Actor.prototype.meetsActionLevelCondition = function(){
    return true
}
Like that:
